subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- August 31, 2026
body:
AcreetionOS resolves geocode-glib update conflict, restoring smooth package updates

If you hit a wall trying to update your system today, you’re not alone. A conflict with the geocode-glib package was blocking updates, but the community has already merged a fix in the 'repair' branch, and work is underway to ensure a clean update path for everyone. This is a classic Arch-based distro headache, and it's good to see it addressed so quickly.

Development
The fix is now in the main branch, and a specific commit targets the conflict on already-installed systems to make the transition seamless. You can always check the official changelog for the precise details on this and other fixes. Meanwhile, Darren has been pushing improvements to the calamares-config, including a tweak to prefer 1080p graphics mode on boot and another to remove mandatory disk encryption for broader hardware compatibility.

Community
On the kernel front, Linux 7.3-rc1 is out, with Linus Torvalds closing the merge window for this release cycle. It's a significant step for those following the bleeding edge. In wider open-source news, Debian voted to allow the "responsible use of generative AI," a decision that sparked plenty of discussion across the community about the future role of AI in software development and governance.

Tip of the day
After applying this geocode-glib fix, it’s always a good practice to run a full system update to ensure all packages are consistent. For new installations or if you’re curious about the configuration changes, the documentation has the latest details on the installer settings. The latest ISOs are always available for download if you want to give the updated system a try.
